title: A finite intermediate algebra capturing finite separable residue subfields
statement: Let $A\to D$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $D$ is integral over $A$, meaning that every element satisfies a monic polynomial over $A$. Let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be prime, put $k=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)$, and suppose the primes of $D$ above $\mathfrak p$ form a finite set $\{\mathfrak r_1,\ldots,\mathfrak r_t\}$ without repetitions (possibly $t=0$). Put $E_i=\operatorname{Frac}(D/\mathfrak r_i)$ with its induced $k$-embedding. For every $i$, suppose a subfield $F_i\subseteq E_i$ containing $k$ is given such that $F_i/k$ is finite-dimensional and separable (minimal polynomials have no repeated roots), and $E_i/F_i$ is purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. There exists a subring $C\subseteq D$ containing the image of $A$, finite as an $A$-module, such that contraction induces a bijection from the primes of $D$ above $\mathfrak p$ to the primes of $C$ above $\mathfrak p$. Writing $\mathfrak s_i=C\cap\mathfrak r_i$, the field $\operatorname{Frac}(C/\mathfrak s_i)$, viewed inside $E_i$ by inclusion, contains $F_i$, is finite-dimensional over $k$, and $E_i/\operatorname{Frac}(C/\mathfrak s_i)$ is purely inseparable. Moreover $D$ is integral over $C$.
